items.excerpt: ETH Zurich researchers built PLATON, a particle detector that uses light-field camera optics and AI to reconstruct invisible particle tracks in 3D inside a single unsegmented block of scintillator. Simulations suggest it could match or surpass today's best detectors while being far simpler to scale.

A BERT-based machine-learning classifier screened 2.6 million cancer papers and flagged more than 250,000 with writing patterns resembling fraudulent 'paper mill' output, published in The BMJ. Suspect papers rose from about 1% in the early 2000s to more than 16% in 2022, exposing a large research-integrity problem.

University of Osaka researchers trained a neural network on molecular-dynamics simulations to evaluate 16 competing structural descriptors of supercooled water. The AI framework pinpointed the most effective ways to distinguish water's two proposed liquid states, one of the field's stubborn mysteries.

EMBL scientists used AI to design NovoTags, small de novo protein tags that bind fluorescent dyes so researchers can track specific proteins inside living cells. An inducible variant, NovoSplit, acts as a molecular switch and could distinguish up to 30 proteins at once by combining emission spectrum and fluorescence lifetime.

Researchers developed an AI-enhanced rare-event sampling framework (AI+RES) that predicts the frequency of extreme heatwaves using up to 1000 times less compute than conventional climate modeling. The AI directs full physics-based models to simulate only the high-probability scenarios, bridging deep-learning efficiency with physical reliability.

A Rutgers-led team built an AI system that continuously monitors mouse locomotor activity and applies machine learning to flag health problems, detecting issues 3-5 days before obvious clinical signs appeared. The tool, reported in Lab Animal, aims to improve welfare and reliability in laboratory animal research.
